title: Adaptive turn-decay prefetch scheduler for mixed prompt/response workloads
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Mixed prompt/response workloads (short prompts followed by long generations and vice versa) cause uneven KV residency and GPU slab fragmentation. Existing continuous batching prioritizes slot utilization but frequently either over-reserves KV pages for long-turn cohorts (wasting memory) or prefetches too late for newly arriving long responses (incurring latency spikes).

Proposal: Implement an adaptive 'turn-decay' prefetch scheduler that tracks per-cohort recent turn-length distributions with exponential decay and uses that signal to drive two coordinated actions: (1) graded KV prefetch windows (small immediate prefetch for high-variance cohorts, larger timed prefetch for cohorts with rising long-turn probability) and (2) progressive slab compaction hinting to the GPU allocator when cohorts shrink. The scheduler ties into the admission controller to softly throttle batch coalescing for cohorts predicted to produce long responses, enabling prioritized KV residency without globally increasing reserved memory.

Design highlights: 
- Per-cohort light-weight histogram: 8-bucket moving window of token-length counts with decay factor alpha configurable by policy.
- Turn-decay predictor: compute P(L>=T) for thresholds T in {64,256,1024} using decayed counts; smooth with EWMA.
- Prefetch policy: map predicted probabilities to a prefetched KV footprint fraction (0-1). Immediate prefetch is allowed up to a small budget; the remainder is scheduled as staggered prefetches to avoid spikes.
- Slab compaction hinting: when decayed occupancy falls below threshold for N seconds, emit a 'shrink' hint to allocator; combine with gentle GC window to avoid oscillation.
- Admission & coalescing integration: if cohort long-turn probability exceeds high-water mark, reduce max coalescing window for those requests to favor lower tail latency.
- Telemetry: expose cohort-level metrics: predicted long-turn probability, prefetched bytes, post-prefetch hit-rate, KV eviction events, per-GPU slab free bytes, and impacted tail-p99 latency.

Why different: Unlike pure length-prioritized batching, this approach anticipates upcoming long generations and coordinates memory hints and admission changes rather than only reordering batches. The turn-decay signal balances responsiveness and stability and reduces thrashing between prefetch and eviction.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce 99th percentile inference latency spikes attributable to late KV fetches by >=30% on mixed workloads (synthetic mix: 30% short->long, 40% medium, 30% long->short) compared to baseline continuous scheduler.
Decrease average KV spill-to-disk events per 10k requests by >=40% in peak periods without increasing average reserved GPU memory above 12% over baseline.
No regression (>2%) in median latency or throughput on stable homogeneous long-turn workloads.
End-to-end rollout toggle via config and observability with cohort-level metrics surfaced in Console.
Automated unit and integration tests covering predictor, prefetch budgets, and allocator hints land in CI with deterministic mocks.
rollout_plan: Feature branch + unit tests -> internal perf bench (small cluster) (canary step: < 5% traffic)
Stage canary: enable scheduler for 5% of production traffic in a single region with elevated monitoring for 72h
Monitor metrics and kill-switch thresholds: p99 latency delta, KV spill count, GPU out-of-memory events. If any threshold is breached, rollback immediately.
Gradual ramp to 25% then 50% with adaptive parameter tuning from observed cohorts, then full rollout if stable.
Post-rollout: 2-week observation period, capture regression reports and follow-up tuning tasks.
test_plan: Synthetic bench: create mixed-turn generators (short->long, long->short, interleaved multi-user chat) to measure p50/p95/p99, KV hit-rate, and GPU slab fragmentation before/after.
Fuzzing: randomized turn-length sequences for 1M requests to validate stability under oscillation and ensure no persistent memory leak.
A/B prod canary: compare cohorts with scheduler on vs off using per-cohort metrics and statistically significant sample sizes for tail latency.
Integration: end-to-end with admission controller, allocator, and KV store mocks to validate hints and backpressure interactions.
Unit: predictor math, decay behavior, mapping table edge cases.
risks_mitigation: Oscillation risk: use hysteresis windows and minimum dwell time before applying shrink hints to allocator to avoid repeated compaction; tune via bench tests.
Over-prefetching: enforce global prefetch budget and per-GPU caps; fall back to LRU eviction policy if budget exhausted.
Complexity: keep predictor state compact (8 buckets + 2 EWMAs) to bound memory and CPU overhead per cohort.
Monitoring blind spots: instrument cohort-level traces and add a forced-sample trace mode to capture full lifecycle when anomalies occur.
notes: Proposed config knobs: runtime.prefetch.decay_alpha, runtime.prefetch.immediate_budget_bytes, runtime.prefetch.slug_window_ms, runtime.slab.shrink_threshold_bytes
